messages:
emily.support: Hey team — customer reported intermittent 401s and high latency after bundling our Node SDK with webpack+esbuild. Happens in production only, but local repro with next.js SSR bundling works sometimes. They also see duplicate POSTs and billing spikes.
liam-frontend: Can you paste the user's package.json + bundler config? quick guess: conditional exports mismatch leads to the app pulling the wrong entry (esm vs cjs) at runtime.
emily.support: Repro steps from customer:
1) npm i @redwood/inference@^2.4.1
2) next build -> next start on Node 18
3) intermittently get 401s from /v1/chat, then client retries, then duplicate requests.
They included this snippet from server console:
```
Error: Unauthorized
at fetch (/workspace/.next/server/chunks/remoteEntry.js:1234:45)
```
support-bot: Logged escalation ID: ESC-2028-911. Adding @axel-eng for packaging guidance.
axel-eng: Thanks — two quick things to check:
- Are they bundling server-side code with an optimizer that rewrites package.json resolution? (Next's server bundle sometimes picks subpath that lacks the typings/credential shim.)
- Do they have NODE_ENV=production + package-lock from older installs? That can change resolution.
liam-frontend: Also look for duplicate runtime copies of the SDK (monorepo hoist or pnpm workspace). If there are two copies, one may have a different exports map and auth shim, causing some requests to use the unauthenticated http client.
jordan-qa: I asked for the minimal repro. They provided a tiny repo link and this package.json for server:
```
{
  "name": "app-server",
  "dependencies": {
    "next": "13.4.4",
    "@redwood/inference": "2.4.1"
  }
}
```
axel-eng: From the repo I saw the bundler output rewriting requires to import the ESM entry but Node resolves to cjs at runtime — the exports map in 2.4.1 had a conditional that missed `node` field. Quick patch: add a forced CJS subpath in the bundler alias or pin `@redwood/inference` to 2.4.3 which has the exports fix.
emily.support: Customer tried pinning to 2.4.3 and the 401s stopped but latency remained higher than expected. Any ideas on the latency spike after retry storms?
axel-eng: The retries multiply requests — if client side doesn't de-duplicate failed in-flight requests, upstream rate limiting/backpressure can increase tail latency. Recommend:
- ensure SDK retry policy uses jittered backoff and circuit breaker (we shipped a fix in 2.5.0)
- enable prefix caching and bundling-safe KV cache on the server
- confirm they are not shipping source maps that block event loop during cold starts
liam-frontend: For a temporary workaround, instruct them to add this to next.config.js to avoid rewriting:
```
module.exports = {
  experimental: { esmExternals: false }
}
```
axel-eng: Filed ENG-PLAT-789 to backport an exports-map warning during install. For now, support send them the pinned version and the next.config tweak — @emily.support can you share the repro and the fix steps with the customer?
emily.support: Will do. I'll also offer to credit the duplicate billing from retry storms while we confirm root cause. Thanks :thumbsup:
